items.q: Yield management aims to maximise the revenue from each impression a publisher sells.
items.why: It balances price, fill and user experience to earn more from the same space.

items.q: Raising a floor price always increases revenue.
items.why: A floor that is too high can leave impressions unsold, so total revenue can fall.

items.q: An ad ops team sets up campaigns, checks delivery and fixes problems.
items.why: Trafficking, quality checks and troubleshooting are daily ad operations work.

items.q: Impression counts from two different systems must always match exactly.
items.why: Small differences are normal because systems count at different moments and with different rules.

items.q: A waterfall calls demand sources one after another in priority order.
items.why: It stops at the first source that fills the slot.

items.q: Unified pricing rules let a publisher set floors that apply across demand sources.
items.why: One rule set avoids different floors for the same impression.

items.q: Sell-through rate is the share of available impressions that were sold.
items.why: Low sell-through means a lot of unsold inventory.

items.q: Ad ops only works inside the ad server and never affects page speed.
items.why: Slow tags and heavy creatives affect page speed, so ad ops watches them too.
